title: How your shop is saved
summary: A Supermarket Simulator shop survives between sessions through a save system of its own: the game keeps a handler, a helper and a root for the file, writes it in chunks, and saves the mess as well as the money.
body: A shop is kept between sessions by a save system of the game's own rather than by the platform holding a snapshot. The game has a handler for the file, a helper around it and a root record, so what is written is structured rather than one undivided block.
The save is written in chunks. The game keeps a record for a chunk of the file, which is how a save can grow with the shop instead of having one fixed size.

Money and stock are not the only things written down. There are separate records for dirt, for dust and for rubbish, so the state of the floor is part of the saved shop rather than being tidied away when you close the game.
A save carries the version it belongs to. The game keeps an updater for its changelog, which is how a file written by an older build can be brought forward when the game changes.
Loading is handled rather than restarted. The game has a hub for resetting the services it shares, which is what lets a saved shop be opened without the whole application being started again.
The file has to restore systems that each keep their own state. Money, the stock and the licences are kept by managers of their own, so a save is a set of parts rather than a single total.
Saving has a picture of its own. The build keeps a canvas for it, which is why writing a shop to disk is something you see rather than only something that happens behind the screen.
The image beside this entry is the game's own: the flash drive it ships as its save media, the same asset the save-slot entry shows, which the manifest records for both.
What this entry does not tell you: how many shops can be saved at once, how large a save file is, or when the game decides to write one. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: The game has a save file handler, a helper around it and a root record of its own.
The save is written in chunks rather than as one block.
Dirt, dust and rubbish each have save records of their own.
The game keeps a changelog updater, so a save can be brought forward when the build changes.
There is a hub for resetting the services the game shares, which is how a saved shop can be loaded without restarting.
Money, the stock and the licences are kept by managers of their own that a save has to restore.
The game ships its own texture for the flash drive a shop is written to.
The build keeps a canvas of its own for saving.

alt.en: The game's own texture for its save media: a retail package holding a black USB flash drive branded DISKORA FlashCore.
alt.zh: 游戏为存档介质准备的贴图：零售包装内一支印着 DISKORA FlashCore 的黑色 U 盘。

alt.en: Diagram: the game writes a save in chunks, including the mess, and reads it back through the services it resets.
alt.zh: 示意图：游戏按块写入存档（含脏乱状态），读取时重置各共享服务。
